notes: No accessibility of W is required for set-bunch factorization.

statement: TC=C intersect W iff every interval-fibration in W is trivial iff W=TF circle TC
notes: Exact recognition hypothesis, separated from smallness.

statement: All sectioned intervals generate all monomorphisms for the total localizer
notes: Empty-to-point cannot be generated; all interval generators preserve emptiness.

statement: All integral-acyclic sectioned intervals generate the integral homology trivial cofibrations on simplicial sets
notes: Finite graph mapping-cylinder counterexample detected by NS3; all five hypotheses and accessibility hold.

statement: The standard simplicial interval with both endpoints is complete for weak homotopy equivalences but not for integral homology equivalences
An accessible presheaf localizer has a set of arbitrary trivial-cofibration generators; adjoining these repairs the interval construction
notes: Thesis 2.3.4; published 1.4.3 and 1.4.4. Does not make pure intervals sufficient.

statement: A set bunch works exactly when it generates the intended localizer and its induced homotopical structure is complete in every slice
notes: Requires both endpoints of a separating interval and set factorization; thesis 2.2.38/44, published 1.3.47/61.

statement: Cisinski thesis and published numbering crosswalk including the absence of an exact thesis counterpart to weak-localizer minimality
notes: Ast 6.1.18 is stronger than thesis Cor5.1.12; Ast 6.1.11 differs in accessibility packaging.

statement: BISITE A27,A28 and PATHS D18 do not supply the missing interval recognition
notes: Earlier precise conclusions retained; only a misapplication to pure intervals is rejected.

statement: For non-total accessible fundamental localizers on sSet all interval generators give the aspherical core; equality with C intersect W iff W proper
notes: A bounded set suffices. Total case is exactly emptiness-preserving monos.

statement: Any set of sectioned intervals can be encoded by its wedge with one chosen section without changing TC or F
notes: The single interval depends on W and on the whole bunch; both endpoint directions survive as pointed retracts.

notes: Yoneda mono y(([0],0))->1 changes support; finite-presentation certificate attached. Properness characterization B.10 is specifically simplicial.

notes: Chaotic C2 category into its fixed terminal cone; direct RLP detector; finite certificate; optional aspherical initial-cone base.
